:::{#cor-deriv-log-chain}

#### Chain rule for logarithms

If $f$ is [differentiable at](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-differentiable) $x$ and $f(x) > 0$, then

$$
\dif{}{x}\logf{f(x)} = \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}
$$

:::

::: proof
Apply @thm-chain-rule and @thm-deriv-log:

$$
\ba
\dif{}{x}\logf{f(x)}
&= f'(x) \cd \dlogf{f(x)}
&& \text{(chain rule, with } g = f \text{ and outer function } \log \text{)}
\\
&= f'(x) \cd \frac{1}{f(x)}
&& \text{(derivative of } \log \text{, valid because } f(x) > 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$
:::
